module _
  {l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (f : A → type-Prop P)
  where

  precomp-Prop :
    {l3 : Level} (Q : Prop l3) →
    (type-Prop P → type-Prop Q) → A → type-Prop Q
  precomp-Prop Q g = g ∘ f

  is-propositional-truncation : Typeω
  is-propositional-truncation =
    {l : Level} (Q : Prop l) → is-equiv (precomp-Prop Q)
blocks.source_note: Replace UU/UUω by Type/Typeω, and expand type-hom-Prop to its underlying function type. This specifies a property of an arbitrary map into a proposition; it does not assert that any truncation exists.

module _
  {l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1}
  (P : Prop l2) (f : A → type-Prop P)
  where

  universal-property-propositional-truncation : Typeω
  universal-property-propositional-truncation =
    {l : Level} (Q : Prop l) (g : A → type-Prop Q) →
    is-contr (Σ ((type-Prop P → type-Prop Q)) (λ h → h ∘ f ＝ g))
blocks.source_note: Replace UU/UUω by Type/Typeω and expand type-hom-Prop. Use equality of functions, exactly as the book's displayed fiber, instead of the source's function-extensionally equivalent homotopy formulation. The following two typed specializations use the already local contractible-map criterion directly.

blocks.code:
abstract
  universal-property-is-propositional-truncation :
    {l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (f : A → type-Prop P) →
    is-propositional-truncation P f →
    universal-property-propositional-truncation P f
  universal-property-is-propositional-truncation P f H Q =
    is-contr-map-is-equiv (H Q)
blocks.source_note: Typed specialization of the existing Theorem 10.4.6 to precomp-Prop P f Q. Its fiber is judgmentally the book's Sigma of extensions with an equality; no transfer to pointwise homotopies is needed. Preserve the explicit truncation hypothesis.

  is-propositional-truncation-universal-property :

blocks.code:
abstract
  map-is-propositional-truncation :
    {l1 l2 l3 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (f : A → type-Prop P) →
    is-propositional-truncation P f →
    (Q : Prop l3) (g : A → type-Prop Q) → (type-Prop P → type-Prop Q)
  map-is-propositional-truncation P f is-ptr-f Q g =
    pr1
      ( center
        ( universal-property-is-propositional-truncation P f is-ptr-f Q g))

  eq-is-propositional-truncation :
    {l1 l2 l3 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (f : A → type-Prop P) →
    (is-ptr-f : is-propositional-truncation P f) →
    (Q : Prop l3) (g : A → type-Prop Q) →
    map-is-propositional-truncation P f is-ptr-f Q g ∘ f ＝ g
  eq-is-propositional-truncation P f is-ptr-f Q g =
    pr2
      ( center
        ( universal-property-is-propositional-truncation P f is-ptr-f Q g))
blocks.source_note: Replace UU by Type and expand type-hom-Prop. Both center projections are unchanged. Rename the second projection from htpy- to eq- and use equality rather than homotopy, matching the preceding identity-based universal property and the book's displayed fiber.

abstract
  is-propositional-truncation-extension-property :
    { l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2)
    ( f : A → type-Prop P) →
    extension-property-propositional-truncation P f →
    is-propositional-truncation P f
  is-propositional-truncation-extension-property P f up-P Q =
    is-equiv-has-converse-is-prop
      ( is-prop-Π (λ x → is-prop-type-Prop Q))
      ( is-prop-Π (λ x → is-prop-type-Prop Q))
      ( up-P Q)

  {l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (f : A → type-Prop P) →

  extension-property-propositional-truncation P f
extension-property-is-propositional-truncation P f H =

module _
  {l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1} {B : Type l2}
  where

  is-prop-equiv-is-prop : is-prop A → is-prop B → is-prop (A ≃ B)
  is-prop-equiv-is-prop H K =
    is-prop-Σ
      ( is-prop-function-type K)
      ( λ f →
        is-prop-product
          ( is-prop-Σ
            ( is-prop-function-type H)
            ( λ g → is-prop-is-contr (is-contr-Π (λ y → K (f (g y)) y))))
          ( is-prop-Σ
            ( is-prop-function-type H)
            ( λ h → is-prop-is-contr (is-contr-Π (λ x → H (h (f x)) x)))))
blocks.source_note: Replace UU by Type. Preserve the full nested-Sigma proof for equivalences between propositions. Its needed Sigma and product proposition lemmas are at Exercise 12.6(a), using the existing embedding criterion; no general is-property-is-equiv or extra Exercise 13.4 solution is needed.

blocks.code:
equiv-is-propositional-truncation :
  {l1 l2 l3 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (P' : Prop l3) →
  (f : A → type-Prop P) (f' : A → type-Prop P') →
  is-propositional-truncation P f → is-propositional-truncation P' f' →
  type-Prop P ≃ type-Prop P'
equiv-is-propositional-truncation P P' f f' H K =
  equiv-iff-is-prop
    ( is-prop-type-Prop P)
    ( is-prop-type-Prop P')
    ( map-is-propositional-truncation P f H P' f')
    ( map-is-propositional-truncation P' f' K P f)
blocks.source_note: Typed specialization of the existing equivalence-from-two-implications theorem to the two extension maps. This is the book's (i)+(ii) implies (iii) proof and supplies both directions of the resulting equivalence explicitly.

blocks.code:
abstract
  is-ptruncation-is-ptruncation-is-equiv :
    {l1 l2 l3 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (P' : Prop l3)
    (f : A → type-Prop P) (f' : A → type-Prop P') (h : (type-Prop P → type-Prop P')) →
    is-equiv h → is-propositional-truncation P f →
    is-propositional-truncation P' f'
  is-ptruncation-is-ptruncation-is-equiv P P' f f' h is-equiv-h is-ptr-f =
    is-propositional-truncation-extension-property P' f'
      ( λ R g →
        ( map-is-propositional-truncation P f is-ptr-f R g) ∘
        ( map-section-is-equiv is-equiv-h))

abstract
  is-ptruncation-is-equiv-is-ptruncation :
    {l1 l2 l3 : Level} {A : Type l1} (P : Prop l2) (P' : Prop l3)
    (f : A → type-Prop P) (f' : A → type-Prop P') (h : (type-Prop P → type-Prop P')) →
    is-propositional-truncation P' f' → is-equiv h →
    is-propositional-truncation P f
  is-ptruncation-is-equiv-is-ptruncation P P' f f' h is-ptr-f' is-equiv-h =
    is-propositional-truncation-extension-property P f
      ( λ R g → (map-is-propositional-truncation P' f' is-ptr-f' R g) ∘ h)
blocks.source_note: Replace UU by Type, expand type-hom-Prop, and rename map-inv-is-equiv to the local map-section-is-equiv. Preserve both remaining implications and their full extension-by-composition proofs. No commutativity assumption is added to the book's statement.

  {l1 l2 : Level} (A : Type l1) (Q : Type l2) →
  is-equiv (precomp (double-negation-introduction {P = A}) (¬¬ Q))
is-equiv-precomp-double-negation A Q =
  is-equiv-has-converse-is-prop
    ( is-prop-function-type is-prop-double-negation)
    ( is-prop-function-type is-prop-double-negation)
    ( double-negation-kleisli-map)

equiv-precomp-double-negation :
  {l1 l2 : Level} (A : Type l1) (Q : Type l2) →
  ((¬¬ A) → (¬¬ Q)) ≃ (A → (¬¬ Q))
pr1 (equiv-precomp-double-negation A Q) =
  precomp (double-negation-introduction {P = A}) (¬¬ Q)
pr2 (equiv-precomp-double-negation A Q) =
  is-equiv-precomp-double-negation A Q
blocks.source_note: Typed application of Proposition 12.1.4's existing converse-map criterion to the book's precomposition map and Exercise 4.3's existing double-negation-kleisli-map. Both function types are propositions by Corollary 13.1.6. Bundle the map and proof using the existing Sigma equivalence representation. This proves only the universal property into doubly negated types, not general propositional truncation or its existence.

  is-prop-Σ :
    {l1 l2 : Level} {A : Type l1} {B : A → Type l2} →
    is-prop A → ((x : A) → is-prop (B x)) → is-prop (Σ A B)
  is-prop-Σ H K =
    is-trunc-is-emb neg-two-𝕋 pr1 (is-emb-pr1-is-subtype K) H

The local is-emb-pr1-is-subtype is exactly is-emb-inclusion-subtype for that family. This is the proposition-level forward implication of Exercise 12.6(a), needed by Proposition 14.1.4.
